title: Eighth Word Religion And Worldly Life Choosing Between Two Roads

questions.question: What does the passage say can help a person understand the world, the human soul, and why religion matters?
questions.answer: Thinking carefully about true religion, especially Islam, helps a person understand these things.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the world like when true religion is missing?
questions.answer: It becomes like a prison.

questions.question: What happens to a human being without religion, according to the passage?
questions.answer: He becomes very miserable.

questions.question: Which two words or statements are said to help solve the mystery of the world and rescue the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Calling on Allah and saying that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: In the comparison, who met the two brothers when the road split?
questions.answer: They met a serious man at the fork in the road.

questions.question: What did the man say about the road on the right?
questions.answer: It had rules and discipline, but it led to safety and happiness.

questions.question: What did the man say about the road on the left?
questions.answer: It had fewer limits, but it led to danger and misery.

questions.question: Which brother chose the right road, and what kind of person was he?
questions.answer: The well-mannered brother chose it, and he had good character.

questions.question: What did the good brother say before taking the right road?
questions.answer: He said that he was trusting in Allah.

questions.question: Why did the other brother choose the left road?
questions.answer: He wanted a path without restrictions.

questions.question: How is the second brother described in the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as immoral and lazy.

questions.question: What important lesson about freedom and rules can be learned from the two roads?
questions.answer: Rules may feel hard at first, but they can protect a person, while doing whatever one wants can lead to harm.

questions.question: What is the main topic introduced at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: It is about understanding life, the human spirit, and the importance of religion.

questions.question: Which religion is clearly named as the true religion before Allah in the passage?
questions.answer: Islam.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah before the comparison begins?
questions.answer: Allah is described as the only true god, ever-living, and sustaining all things.

questions.question: Why does the passage invite the reader to listen to a comparison?
questions.answer: Because the comparison helps explain the value of religion and the condition of people with or without it.

questions.question: Where were the two brothers going when the story began?
questions.answer: They were on a long journey.

questions.question: What happened that forced them to make a choice?
questions.answer: The road divided into two paths.

questions.question: What warning and promise were connected to the right path?
questions.answer: It required obedience to order, but it brought safety and happiness.

questions.question: What warning was connected to the left path?
questions.answer: Its freedom came with danger and unhappiness.

questions.question: What does the good brother’s choice show about his character?
questions.answer: It shows that he was willing to accept discipline and trust Allah.

questions.question: What does the other brother’s choice show about his character?
questions.answer: It shows that he cared more about doing whatever he wanted than about what was right or safe.

questions.question: The left road looked easier at first. In the end of the passage, how is that road described?
questions.answer: It only seemed easy on the outside, but it was really heavy and difficult.

questions.question: Why does the passage say “we shall follow this man” on the left road?
questions.answer: It is preparing the reader to watch what happens to the brother who made the wrong choice.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the connection between religion and understanding life?
questions.answer: It teaches that true religion helps a person understand life and himself.

questions.question: According to the passage, what frees the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Turning to Allah and affirming His oneness frees it from darkness.

questions.question: In the story, what do the two roads seem to represent?
questions.answer: They represent two ways of life: one with faith, order, and safety, and one with selfish freedom and harm.

questions.question: What kind of person would be more likely to choose the right road in this passage?
questions.answer: A person with good character who accepts guidance.

questions.question: What kind of person would be more likely to choose the left road in this passage?
questions.answer: A person who is careless, morally weak, and dislikes rules.

questions.question: What did the serious man leave up to the brothers?
questions.answer: He left the final choice to them.

questions.question: How did the brother on the right respond after hearing the advice?
questions.answer: He trusted Allah and followed the path with order.

questions.question: How did the brother on the left respond after hearing the advice?
questions.answer: He chose the path without restrictions.

questions.question: Why is the right path not described as completely easy?
questions.answer: Because it includes laws and discipline that require effort.

questions.question: Why is the left path not truly a better path even though it offers freedom?
questions.answer: Because that kind of freedom leads to danger and sadness.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about obeying good rules?
questions.answer: It suggests that good rules protect people and lead them to good results.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person can understand by thinking about religion properly?
questions.answer: A person can understand the world, the soul, and the worth of religion for human life.

questions.question: How is a life without true religion pictured in the passage?
questions.answer: It is pictured as dark, painful, and trapped.

questions.question: What role do the words about Allah play in the passage?
questions.answer: They are shown as keys that help solve life’s deep mystery and bring light to the soul.

questions.question: What setting is used to teach this lesson?
questions.answer: A story about two brothers traveling and choosing between two roads.

questions.question: What happened when the brothers reached the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They asked a stern-looking man which road was good.

questions.question: How did the man compare the two roads?
questions.answer: He said one had discipline with good results, and the other had unchecked freedom with bad results.

questions.question: What made the good brother different from the other one before he even chose?
questions.answer: He had better manners and character.

questions.question: What prayerful attitude did the good brother show?
questions.answer: He showed reliance on Allah.

questions.question: What desire pushed the other brother to the left road?
questions.answer: He wanted to avoid limits and responsibilities.

questions.question: What contrast is given between appearance and reality in the last sentence of the target passage?
questions.answer: The left road looked comfortable at first, but it was actually difficult and heavy.

questions.question: What big message can a student learn from the two brothers’ choices?
questions.answer: A right path may ask for self-control, but it brings goodness, while careless freedom can bring trouble.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the religion accepted before Allah?
questions.answer: Islam is the religion accepted before Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person should understand about the world if there is no true religion?
questions.answer: The world becomes like a prison.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the condition of a person without religion?
questions.answer: That person becomes deeply unhappy.

questions.question: What is one reason the comparison of the two brothers is important?
questions.answer: It shows the difference between following guidance and following desires.

questions.question: What choice did the brothers have to make?
questions.answer: They had to choose between a right-hand road and a left-hand road.

questions.question: What was the cost of taking the right-hand road?
questions.answer: A person had to obey rules and order.

questions.question: What was the reward of taking the right-hand road?
questions.answer: Safety and happiness.

questions.question: What was attractive about the left-hand road at first?
questions.answer: It seemed free and unrestricted.

questions.question: What was hidden inside that seeming freedom?
questions.answer: Danger and misery.

questions.question: Which brother acted with trust in Allah?
questions.answer: The brother with good character did.

questions.question: What mistake did the other brother make when choosing his road?
questions.answer: He chose based only on having no restrictions.

questions.question: What subjects does the passage say a person can understand through its lesson?
questions.answer: The world, the human spirit, the value of religion, and the condition of life without true religion.

questions.question: What does the passage say rescues the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Remembering Allah and declaring His oneness.

questions.question: What kind of story method is used to explain the lesson?
questions.answer: A comparison is used.

questions.question: Who are the main people in the comparison?
questions.answer: Two brothers on a journey.

questions.question: What information did the man at the fork give about the right road?
questions.answer: It required obedience, but it brought protection and joy.

questions.question: What information did he give about the left road?
questions.answer: It allowed more freedom, but it led to harm and sadness.

questions.question: Why was the good brother ready to take the right road?
questions.answer: He had good character and trusted Allah.

questions.question: Why did the other brother prefer the left road?
questions.answer: He wanted a life without limits.

questions.question: Which road would best match a person who follows Allah’s guidance even when it is hard?
questions.answer: The right road.

questions.question: Which road would best match a person who follows his desires just because it feels easy?
questions.answer: The left road.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about choosing a path only because it looks easy?
questions.answer: It can be a bad choice because what looks easy may actually lead to hardship.

questions.question: What is one main lesson of the target passage for a Muslim student?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah and following right guidance lead to good, while rejecting guidance for selfish freedom leads to harm.
